szoveg_eredeti:
The recently proclaimed parable of the 10 bridesmaids waiting with burning lamps to meet the bridegroom offers insights as we respond to the development of artificial intelligence.

In the story, Jesus talks about 10 bridesmaids waiting for the bridegroom. Five were wise, and five were foolish. They have much in common. All 10 showed up, all 10 brought lamps and all 10 fell asleep as the groom was delayed. But the crucial difference was that five brought an extra supply of oil, while the other five brought only enough to keep up momentary appearances.

At midnight, when they hear the cry, “Behold, the bridegroom! Come out to meet him!” five maidens realized their lamps were flickering out. They asked the others for some of their oil, and they replied, “No, for there may not be enough for us and for you. Go instead to the merchants and buy some for yourselves.”

While they were away, the bridegroom arrived, the door was locked, and when they knocked, the groom spoke those chilling words: “Amen, I say to you, I do not know you.”

We might conclude that the message of this parable is “be prepared” for the Lord’s return or the end of our earthly life. But if we look deeper, the oil represents something indispensable: the deep, interior substance of our faith, our moral readiness and the love we cultivate in our souls.

This spiritual foundation cannot be borrowed, outsourced or faked at the last minute. It is what keeps the light of truth burning when the long night of waiting tests our resolve.

Today, as we stand at the breathtaking threshold in human history with the rise and rapid integration of artificial intelligence into every facet of our lives, this parable speaks to our generation with urgent clarity.

Artificial intelligence is perhaps the most powerful tool humanity has ever fashioned. It can analyze vast medical datasets to potentially cure diseases, model climate change for possible solutions and catalogue human knowledge at speeds previously unimaginable.

And yet, if we are not vigilant, we risk becoming like the five foolish bridesmaids, captivated by the bright, immediate shine of new lamps, while neglecting the essential oil that keeps our humanity alive. What is that oil, the spiritual foundation that cannot be borrowed, outsourced or faked? In the realm of ethics and technological progress, it is the absolute, unshakable commitment to human dignity.

Human dignity is not something an algorithm can compute, measure or generate. It is the divine reality that every single human being is created in the “imago Dei,” the image and likeness of God, from the unborn child to the frail elderly, from the laborer whose job is displaced to the migrant seeking refuge.

Our worth does not come from our productivity, our data output, our economic efficiency or our technological literacy. Our worth is given to us by our Creator, paid for on the cross and sealed by the Holy Spirit.

The great danger of our technological age is that in the rush to adopt AI, our government and corporations prioritize speed, profit and convenience over the sacred value of the human person. When algorithms determine who receives a loan, who gets healthcare access, who is flagged by justice systems or how war is waged, we face a profound moral crossroads.

If an AI system optimizes cold efficiency at the expense of fairness, compassion and human oversight, it burns without oil. If we allow technology to isolate us, to substitute machine logic for human empathy, or to treat human beings as mere data points to be processed, our lamps will run dry in the middle of the night.

In his encyclical “Magnifica Humanitas,” Pope Leo calls for a new ethical framework, rooted in the service of the human family. “More power,” he observes, “does not necessarily imply something better. In this respect, the words of Romano Guardini remain relevant: ‘Contemporary man has not been trained to use power well’” (MH 93).

The point is that technology must serve humanity, not the other way around. AI must be a tool that enhances human agency, solidarity and the common good, never a replacement for the human heart.

We each have a role in advocating for the principle of human dignity to remain at the center of this new digital landscape.

First, we must promote policies and designs that keep human dignity at the center of innovation by insisting on human supremacy in moral decisions. No machine should ever make life-and-death choices or replace the irreplaceable role of human conscience and mercy, especially when it comes to medicine and war.

Second, priority must be given to protecting the weak and vulnerable. History has shown that whenever new technology emerges, it is often the poor, the elderly and the marginalized who are left behind or exploited. A truly wise society measures technological progress not by how much wealth it creates for the tech-savvy, but by how it lifts up the least among us.

Finally, as the image of the wise bridesmaids possessing a deep supply of oil suggests, each of us must personally cultivate our interior lives. The foolish bridesmaids thought they could buy what they needed at the last moment. But no one can download wisdom. We cannot algorithmically generate character, empathy or holiness.

In an age of automated responses and instant answers, we must guard our capacity for silence, for deep prayer, for genuine human relationship, and for the quiet work of love that no machine can ever perform.

Jesus, the Second Vatican Council reminds us, is always coming into our lives, always present, always exercising his priestly ministry. He encounters us today in our worship but also in the faces of our brothers and sisters.

When he comes, the question will be, will we be ready to greet him, holding bright, hollow lamps, dazzled by our own inventions, or will he find us rich in the oil of love, justice and respect for every human life?

May God grant us the wisdom to build a future where technological power never stands above the sanctity of human dignity.

prioritas.indok: Vallási jellegű véleménycikk a mesterséges intelligenciáról
prioritas.cim_hu: Bibliai példázattal elemzi az MI kihívásait egy katolikus elemzés
prioritas.lead_hu: Egy vallási elemzés a tíz szűzről szóló evangéliumi példázat segítségével vizsgálja az emberiség erkölcsi felkészültségét a mesterséges intelligencia terjedésének korában.
